item.title: Codex Sidebar partially incompatible with TRAE (Explorer/Folders cannot be moved and Open Codex Sidebar fails)
item.body:
Title: Codex Sidebar partially incompatible with TRAE (Explorer/Folders cannot be moved and Open Codex Sidebar fails)

### Environment

* TRAE: 1.107.1
* Codex Extension (openai.chatgpt): 26.601.20914
* Linux Mint 22.3 Cinnamon
* x64

### Description

The Codex extension works correctly when using:

* Codex: New Codex Agent
* Codex: New Thread in Codex Sidebar

However, there are layout and sidebar compatibility issues when using Codex inside TRAE.

### Issues Found

#### 1. Open Codex Sidebar error

Running:

```text
Codex: Open Codex Sidebar
```

produces:

```text
command 'chatgpt.openSidebar' not found
```

The Codex extension is installed, updated and operational. The problem appears to be related to sidebar integration.

#### 2. Explorer/Folders cannot be moved

TRAE provides the command:

```text
View: Move View
```

However, native views such as:

* Explorer
* Folders
* Open Editors

do not appear in the list of movable views.

Only extension-provided views are listed.

Because of this, it is not possible to separate:

```text
Left Sidebar:
- Codex

Right Sidebar:
- Explorer
```

even though Secondary Sidebar is available and working.

#### 3. Secondary Sidebar compatibility

Secondary Sidebar can be enabled successfully.

Codex can appear in the sidebar, but Explorer/Folders remain locked to the primary sidebar container and cannot be reassigned.

### Expected Behavior

Allow native Explorer/Folders views to be moved between Primary Sidebar and Secondary Sidebar, similar to VS Code.

Allow Codex Sidebar to open without relying on the missing command:

```text
chatgpt.openSidebar
```

### Current Behavior

* Codex Agent works.
* Codex chat works.
* Secondary Sidebar works.
* Explorer cannot be moved.
* Open Codex Sidebar fails with command not found.

### Additional Notes

This behavior appears to be specific to TRAE. The same functionality is available in standard VS Code through movable views and secondary sidebar support.
